summary: Same 5-section beat-driven meter with matching section geometry, bar dynamics and 3-section mode once both have settled, but the port's auto-gain warm-up runs the opposite direction, its hue cycle is ~2.3x too fast with a non-mirrored per-section hue spread, and its Decay dial is dead.
observations: Rig: 60-px strip, both sides fed the identical beat120 synthetic sensor signal (meta.json: wantsSensors true, sensors "synth" on both). With --sensors off both sides render exactly black (mean 0, motion 0) — identical graceful-degradation behaviour.

SETTLED STEADY STATE (skip 60 s, 20 fps) is a strong match. --dump across one beat at t=80.0-80.45 s gives near-identical spatial layout on both: section 1 bar at px 0-3, section 2 at 13-22, section 3 at 26-33, section 4 at 41-42, section 5 at 56-59, each growing symmetrically about its own anchor on the 2 Hz beat and decaying over ~0.3-0.4 s. Widths agree within ~1 px, and both show the same beat-locked 'spiky' waterfall texture.

WARM-UP TRANSIENT IS INVERTED. --seconds 120 at fps 10/20/40: the original starts railed at full scale — every one of its 5 sections lit end-to-end (all pixels 254, dump at t=1.0-4.45 s shows literally no beat modulation, only hue changing) — and its auto-gain relaxes into the settled look only around FRAME ~1050 (t=104.5 s @10 fps, 54.8 s @20 fps, 26.2 s @40 fps, i.e. frame-count based, fps-independent in frames). Mean brightness per 100-frame block, orig: 117,96,116,110,95,99,95,108,83,90,77,51,48,50,38,45,... The port has no such phase: it is already at settled deflection at frame 0 and creeps UP into place (20,23,24,25,30,...,37,38,41). Both converge (orig ~45, port ~37), but for the first ~1000 frames the original is a fully-lit strip and the port is 5 thin bars on black.

Hue cycling: both sides sweep hue as a TRIANGLE wave (up then back down, not a sawtooth). Original half-period ~24.5 s (settled, px-tracked: hue 0.47->0.96 over t=60-74 s then 0.93->0.04 over t=76-98 s, |rate| ~0.041/s). Port half-period ~10.5 s (|rate| ~0.085/s) — about 2.3x too fast. Both are fps-invariant (10/20/40 fps hue readings identical), so no frame-rate coupling on either side.

Per-section hue offset is distributed differently. Original: hue is MIRRORED about the strip centre — at StaticColor=1/Color=0.5 the five sections read 0.28, 0.31, 0.32, 0.31, 0.28 (spread 0.04); free-running it reads s1 0.47, s3 0.50, s5 0.47. Port: hue is a MONOTONIC left-to-right ramp — 0.33, 0.37, 0.41, 0.45, 0.49 (spread 0.16, 4x the original's), free-running s1 0.79, s3 0.86, s5 0.92. Port also sits ~+0.10 hue above the original for the same Color value.

Control SURFACE mismatch: 5 of 10 names/labels differ. orig sliderBassBalance/'BassBalance' vs port sliderBass/'Bass'; sliderLowMidBalance/'LowMidBalance' vs sliderLowMid/'LowMid'; sliderMidsBalance/'MidsBalance' vs sliderMid/'Mid'; sliderTrebBalance/'TrebBalance' vs sliderTreble/'Treble'; toggle3Sections/'3Sections' vs toggleThreeSections/'ThreeSections'. toggleStaticColor, sliderColor, sliderBlending, sliderDecay and gaugeSensitivity match in name and kind; counts and kinds are otherwise identical.
ThreeSections toggle matches well on both: strip collapses to two 2-px end sections plus one wide centre bar spanning roughly px 20-40, pulsing symmetrically about px 29.5.
Pattern is fully deterministic — seed 7 reproduces seed 1's stats exactly (orig mean 45 / port 36 over t=60-80 s), so no RNG-character judgement was needed.
Neither side dies: over 120 s at 40 fps the last quarter averages meanBrightness 44.8 (orig) / 41.2 (port) with motion ~3-4 on both.

dials.name: toggleStaticColor + sliderColor
dials.origEffect: StaticColor=1 freezes the hue walk; hue tracks the Color slider (0.25->~0.02, 0.5->~0.30, 0.8->~0.66) with only a small +-0.02 spread across sections, mirrored about strip centre
dials.portEffect: same freeze and same direction, but offset ~+0.07..+0.21 in hue (0.25->~0.07, 0.5->~0.40, 0.8->~0.87) and with a much larger monotonic spread across sections (0.16 vs 0.04)

dials.name: sliderDecay
dials.origEffect: Live and strong. 0 = peak-hold: bars pin at ~6-7 px per section and stop moving (meanB 64.2, motion 1.6 over a 20 s settled window). 1 = fast decay: dimmer and more dynamic (meanB 44.7, motion 2.7). Probe maxDelta 43.20.
dials.portEffect: Effectively inert over the same 20 s / 40-beat settled window: meanB 35.2 / 36.5 / 37.8 and motion 4.2 / 4.3 / 4.1 at 0 / 0.5 / 1 — no peak-hold at 0, bars keep pulsing identically. Probe maxDelta 1.91.

dials.name: sliderBlending
dials.origEffect: 0 = hard-edged bars (no shoulders); 1 = soft shoulders bleeding 1-2 px past each bar edge
dials.portEffect: same direction and comparable magnitude — hard edges at 0, 1-2 px soft shoulders at 1

dials.name: toggle3Sections / toggleThreeSections
dials.origEffect: collapses 5 sections into 3: two 11-px end sections plus one 36-px middle; middle bar pulses symmetrically about px 29.5
dials.portEffect: same 3-section collapse, same centre, middle bar width within ~2 px of the original's across the beat

dials.name: sliderBassBalance / sliderBass
dials.origEffect: drives the two OUTER sections. Isolated (bass=1, other three=0) avg lit px per section = [9.2, 5.2, 3.8, 0.0, 9.2]; bass=0 shrinks the outer sections and lets 2/3/4 saturate.
dials.portEffect: same mapping — isolated bass=1 gives [6.3, 2.4, 3.4, 0.0, 6.3]; direction and section assignment match, magnitude ~30% lower

dials.name: sliderLowMidBalance / sliderLowMid
dials.origEffect: INERT over an 8 s / 16-beat settled window: with the other three at 0, LowMid=1 gives avg lit px [4.1, 10.0, 8.8, 5.6, 4.1] — byte-identical to all-four-at-zero. Dial effect unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: clearly live and mapped to section 4: LowMid=1 (others 0) gives [1.1, 3.2, 4.6, 5.6, 1.1] vs [1.5, 4.0, 5.0, 1.8, 1.5] at all-zero

dials.name: sliderMidsBalance / sliderMid
dials.origEffect: live but broad — Mids=1 (others 0) saturates sections 2, 3 AND 4 together: [3.4, 10.0, 10.0, 10.0, 3.4]

dials.name: sliderTrebBalance / sliderTreble
dials.origEffect: INERT over the same 8 s settled window: Treb=1 (others 0) gives [4.1, 10.0, 8.8, 5.8, 4.1], indistinguishable from all-zero and from LowMid=1. Dial effect unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: live and mapped to section 2: Treble=1 (others 0) gives [1.0, 10.0, 4.0, 0.0, 1.0]

dials.name: gaugeSensitivity
dials.origEffect: display-only gauge, not probed; its behaviour is visible indirectly as the ~1050-frame auto-gain relaxation described above
dials.portEffect: display-only gauge, not probed; port shows no equivalent relaxation

feedback: Auto-gain start point is inverted. The original boots with its meter railed — all 5 sections lit end-to-end, no beat modulation visible at all, mean brightness ~117 — and its gain relaxes DOWNWARD over roughly 1000 render frames (measured at frames ~1050 for the crossover at 10, 20 and 40 fps alike, so it is frame-counted, not time-based) until the strip settles at mean ~45 with thin beat bars. The port starts already near the settled deflection (mean ~20) and creeps UPWARD to ~38. Initialise the sensitivity/gain state so the first ~1000 frames are over-deflected (bars pinned to full section width) and let it fall into place, rather than starting under-deflected.

Hue cycle is ~2.3x too fast. Both sides sweep hue as a triangle wave, but the original's half-period is ~24.5 s (|d(hue)/dt| ~0.041/s, measured at 20 fps in the settled regime, and identical at 10 and 40 fps) while the port's is ~10.5 s (~0.085/s). Slow the port's hue advance by a factor of ~2.3; the triangle shape and fps-invariance are already right.

Per-section hue offsets must MIRROR about the strip centre, not ramp across it. Original at StaticColor=1/Color=0.5: sections read hue 0.28, 0.31, 0.32, 0.31, 0.28 — symmetric, total spread 0.04. Port reads 0.33, 0.37, 0.41, 0.45, 0.49 — a monotonic ramp with spread 0.16. Make the offset depend on distance from centre (like the bass-at-both-ends section layout already does) and shrink it to about a quarter of its current size.

Static colour is offset. For the same sliderColor the port's hue sits ~+0.10 above the original (Color 0.25: orig ~0.02 vs port ~0.07; Color 0.5: orig ~0.30 vs port ~0.40; Color 0.8: orig ~0.66 vs port ~0.87). Re-base the mapping so Color=0.5 lands near hue 0.30.

The Decay dial does nothing on the port. Over a 20 s / 40-beat settled window the port posts meanBrightness 35.2 / 36.5 / 37.8 and motion 4.2 / 4.3 / 4.1 at Decay 0 / 0.5 / 1. The original at Decay=0 goes into a visible peak-HOLD — every section pins at ~6-7 px and the strip stops animating (motion drops to 1.6, brightness rises to 64) — and at Decay=1 it is dimmer and livelier (44.7 / 2.7). Wire Decay to the bar fall-off rate so that 0 holds peaks indefinitely and 1 drops them within a beat.

Frequency-band-to-section mapping differs for the three non-bass sliders. Bass is right on both (drives the two outer sections). But on the original, isolating MidsBalance=1 saturates sections 2, 3 and 4 together ([3.4, 10, 10, 10, 3.4]) whereas the port's Mid drives only section 3 ([1.0, 3.0, 7.8, 2.0, 1.0]); and the original's LowMidBalance and TrebBalance produce output byte-identical to all-sliders-zero over a 16-beat settled window (they appear to be no-ops in the original) while the port's LowMid and Treble visibly drive sections 4 and 2 respectively. Widen the port's Mid to cover sections 2-4 to match; the extra liveness on LowMid/Treble is a smaller issue but should be checked against the original's intent.

Rename the five diverging controls to the original's names/labels: sliderBass->sliderBassBalance ('BassBalance'), sliderLowMid->sliderLowMidBalance ('LowMidBalance'), sliderMid->sliderMidsBalance ('MidsBalance'), sliderTreble->sliderTrebBalance ('TrebBalance'), toggleThreeSections->toggle3Sections ('3Sections').

Everything else is already right and should not be disturbed: 5-section geometry (bars at px 0-3 / 13-22 / 26-33 / 41-42 / 56-59), symmetric bar growth, the ~0.3-0.4 s decay envelope on the 2 Hz beat, the ThreeSections layout, the Blending shoulder behaviour, the Bass->outer-sections mapping, and black output with dead sensors.
